## TL;DR

The stale-evidence notice and Refresh evidence button stay hidden on the review card and in the drawer while the task's close-out is queued or running, and return if the job fails. The notice reads "Stale evidence" with no `repoos verify` text. The server also refuses `repoos verify` and both automatic refresh paths while this task's own job is queued, not only while a close-out is running. The UI capture now highlights the footer where the prompt used to be, on a genuinely queued fixture.

## Work and rationale

The card and drawer had two gates that ignored the pipeline. The card's stale block was gated on `status === "review"` and a `STALE-EVIDENCE-ONLY` verdict (`staleEvidenceOnly` in `TaskCard.vue`). The drawer's Refresh evidence button was gated on `status === "review"` alone.

I added one shared rule in `src/ui-app/src/lib/integration-pipeline-ui.ts`: `integrationEvidencePromptHidden(snap, taskId)`. It is true when `integrationPipelineRole` reports the task as `queued`, or as `active` with a non-failed job. Non-terminal job phases are exactly `queued`, `syncing`, `validating`, `publishing` and `cleanup`, so the role check covers the acceptance criteria without listing phases. A failed job drops out of the role, so the prompt returns after a failure.

The card uses the helper inside `staleEvidenceOnly`, so the whole block goes. The drawer adds an `evidencePromptHidden` computed and gates the button on it. I did not reuse the drawer's `inPipeline`: it ignores `failed`, and changing it would alter the "Integrating…" UI.

Server side, `refreshTaskEvidence` in `src/server/routes/tasks.ts` checked only `closeOutLock.closingOut()`, which is set while a close-out runs, not while its job waits in the queue. The review round caught this. I added `taskCloseOutPending(coordinator, taskId)` in `src/server/integration-job.ts`. It is per-task: the repo-wide `closeOutPending` is true for any queued job, which would block every other task's refresh. The verify route refuses with `closingOutRefusal(id)`. `automaticStaleEvidenceRefresh` and `automaticEvidenceGapRepair` take an optional `closeOutQueued(taskId)` dep and check it beside the global lock, both before capture and under the locks. `server.ts` passes `taskCloseOutPending(jobCoordinator, id)`. The dep is optional so callers without a coordinator keep the global lock.

The shot had three problems across rounds:

1. Auto-capture of `/` hit a redirect to `/work`. I declared a shot on `/work` instead.
2. The first declared shot used a `selector`, which made the capture wait for an animated card to settle, and it timed out at 5 s. I removed the selector and kept a highlight.
3. The fixture was a `validating` active job, not a queued one, and the review asked for a genuinely queued card with its footer visible. The fixture is now a queued task behind another task's running close-out. The integration bar is collapsed (as in the `integration:median15` fixture) so its popover does not cover the footer. The highlight is `[data-task-id="9999"] .tc-card-footer-action`, which is the footer action that now shows in place of the prompt.

A fixture task (9998) for the running close-out had no branch, so its card requested `handoff-status` for an id the server does not know, and the UI gate failed with 404. It now has an empty branch, as the other fixture cards do (#0768).

The CLI is unchanged; `repoos verify` gets the new 409 from the server.

## Approaches tried

I considered gating on phase names directly. That needs a second list that can drift from `JobPhase`, and the non-terminal phases are those five, so "in the pipeline and not failed" is equivalent with less to maintain.

I considered reusing `closeOutPending` for the server guard. It is true when any job is queued, so one task's queue entry would block evidence refresh everywhere. A per-task predicate is the right scope.

## Challenges and blockers

Several scoped `repoos check` runs were stopped when earlier sessions ended, and the machine was carrying many other `repoos check` processes, which slowed the capture. I re-ran the check until it produced a clean result. The branch's WIP checkpoint commits are expected per AGENTS.md.

Main has moved since the branch point. The only conflict is this task's own `work/1277-*.md`, which RepoOS resolves. I did not merge main or commit, because the runner rules say not to run git add or commit.

I did not reproduce the browser capture headlessly in this session; the shot's behaviour is inferred from the capture code and the fixture tests, which pass.

## Key learnings

- A "hide while in pipeline" check must decide whether a failed job still counts. The drawer's `inPipeline` treats a failed active job as in pipeline; the card's does not. Both are used elsewhere, so I wrote a separate rule.
- A queue guard must be scoped to the task. A repo-wide "any job queued" answer would block unrelated tasks.
- A declared shot with a `selector` waits for that element to settle; animated cards need a page capture with a highlight instead.
- Fixture tasks need an empty branch, or their cards request endpoints the server does not know.
- `needs-input-ui.ts` still tells users to run `repoos verify <id>` in a needs-input message. That is a different surface, so I left it.
